headline: Argentina Country Risk Index Rises to 918 Points
summary: Argentina's country risk index increased by 66 points to 918 on Thursday, reaching its highest level since late October 2025. The rise followed a decline in both government bonds and stocks.
why: The country risk index measures the spread between local sovereign bonds and US Treasuries, reflecting investor perception of the risk of default.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Rising country risk indicates higher perceived probability of default.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Falling bond prices directly increase the yield spread, which is the primary component of the country risk index.
